## Business question

Late departures cost airlines crew time, missed connections and unhappy passengers. **Which flights leaving New York leave late, and how much of that is down to the weather rather than things the airline controls, like the time of day a flight is scheduled?**

**Data:** every flight that left JFK, LaGuardia and Newark in 2023 (U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics), with hourly weather at each airport (Iowa Environmental Mesonet), from the `nycflights23` R package.

A flight counts as **late** if it left 15 minutes or more after its scheduled time, the standard used by the U.S. Department of Transportation.

## 1. Setup

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)     # dplyr, ggplot2, forcats, tidyr
library(nycflights23)  # flights, weather, airlines
library(broom)         # tidy model output

dir.create("charts", showWarnings = FALSE)

orange <- "#e8603c"
navy   <- "#13263f"
grey   <- "#c9ced6"
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## 2. Load and check the data

```{r load}
cat("Flights:", nrow(flights), " Weather hours:", nrow(weather),
    " Airlines:", nrow(airlines), "\n")

# A flight with no departure time never left: it was cancelled
summary_counts <- flights |>
  summarise(flights   = n(),
            cancelled = sum(is.na(dep_time)),
            pct_cancelled = round(100 * cancelled / flights, 1))
summary_counts

# Keep flights that left, and mark the late ones
departed <- flights |>
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay)) |>
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") |>
  rename(airline = name) |>
  mutate(late = dep_delay >= 15)

departed |>
  summarise(departed = n(),
            pct_late = round(100 * mean(late), 1),
            avg_delay_mins = round(mean(dep_delay), 1),
            median_delay_mins = median(dep_delay))
```

**Check:** 435,352 flights, 10,738 cancelled (2.5%); of the 424,614 that left, 21.6% were late. The median delay is negative: most flights leave a little early.

## 3. When are flights late?

### Delays build up through the day

```{r by-hour, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
by_hour <- departed |>
  group_by(hour) |>
  summarise(flights = n(), pct_late = 100 * mean(late)) |>
  filter(flights >= 1000)          # leaves out hours with very few flights
by_hour |> mutate(pct_late = round(pct_late, 1)) |> print(n = Inf)

p_hour <- ggplot(by_hour, aes(x = hour, y = pct_late)) +
  geom_col(fill = orange, width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(pct_late)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 5:22, labels = \(h) paste0(h, ":00")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "The later in the day a flight is scheduled, the more likely it leaves late",
       subtitle = "Share of departures 15+ minutes late, by scheduled hour, NYC airports 2023",
       x = "Scheduled departure", y = "Late (%)",
       caption = "Source: U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics via nycflights23") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
p_hour
ggsave("charts/late_by_hour.png", p_hour, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
```

### Airlines and airports

```{r by-airline, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5}
by_airline <- departed |>
  group_by(airline) |>
  summarise(flights = n(), pct_late = 100 * mean(late)) |>
  filter(flights >= 5000) |>
  arrange(pct_late)
by_airline |> mutate(pct_late = round(pct_late, 1))

p_airline <- ggplot(by_airline, aes(x = pct_late, y = reorder(airline, pct_late))) +
  geom_col(fill = navy, width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct_late, 1), "%")), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Share of departures 15+ minutes late, by airline",
       subtitle = "Airlines with at least 5,000 departures from NYC in 2023",
       x = "Late (%)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics via nycflights23")
p_airline
ggsave("charts/late_by_airline.png", p_airline, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 150, bg = "white")

departed |>
  group_by(origin) |>
  summarise(flights = n(), pct_late = round(100 * mean(late), 1))
```

## 4. How much does the weather matter?

Each flight is matched to the weather at its airport in the hour it was scheduled to leave.

```{r weather}
with_weather <- departed |>
  inner_join(weather |> select(origin, time_hour, precip, visib, wind_speed),
             by = c("origin", "time_hour")) |>
  drop_na(precip, visib, wind_speed) |>
  mutate(rain        = precip > 0,
         low_vis     = visib < 3,          # under 3 miles of visibility
         strong_wind = wind_speed >= 20)   # 20 mph or more

cat("Flights matched to weather:", nrow(with_weather), "\n")

weather_effect <- bind_rows(
  with_weather |> group_by(condition = if_else(rain, "Yes", "No")) |>
    summarise(flights = n(), pct_late = 100 * mean(late)) |> mutate(factor = "Rain"),
  with_weather |> group_by(condition = if_else(low_vis, "Yes", "No")) |>
    summarise(flights = n(), pct_late = 100 * mean(late)) |> mutate(factor = "Visibility under 3 miles"),
  with_weather |> group_by(condition = if_else(strong_wind, "Yes", "No")) |>
    summarise(flights = n(), pct_late = 100 * mean(late)) |> mutate(factor = "Wind 20 mph or more")
)
weather_effect |> mutate(pct_late = round(pct_late, 1))

p_weather <- ggplot(weather_effect, aes(x = pct_late, y = factor, fill = condition)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct_late), "%")),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(No = grey, Yes = orange)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Bad weather raises the share of late departures",
       subtitle = "Share of departures 15+ minutes late, by weather in the scheduled hour",
       x = "Late (%)", y = NULL, fill = "Condition present",
       caption = "Source: BTS and Iowa Environmental Mesonet via nycflights23") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
p_weather
ggsave("charts/late_by_weather.png", p_weather, width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
```

Delays build up through the day: 8.9% of flights scheduled at 6:00 left late, against 32.5% at 19:00. Airlines differed widely, from 12.5% late for Republic Airline to 32.3% for JetBlue, and LaGuardia (18.7%) did better than Newark (23.4%) and JFK (23.1%). Bad weather also went with more late departures: 29.5% in rain against 20.2% in dry hours, 32.6% when visibility was under 3 miles and 30.8% in winds of 20 mph or more. But bad weather is rare: only 49,499 of 406,779 flights (12%) left in rain.

## 5. Separating time of day from the weather

Evening flights and stormy afternoons overlap, so the simple comparisons above can mix the two up. A logistic regression estimates the effect of each factor while holding the others constant: time of day, airline, airport, month, rain, low visibility and strong wind.

```{r model}
model_data <- with_weather |>
  mutate(period  = cut(hour, breaks = c(0, 9, 12, 15, 18, 24), right = FALSE,
                       labels = c("5-8am", "9-11am", "12-2pm", "3-5pm", "6pm+")),
         airline = fct_lump_min(airline, min = 5000, other_level = "Other airlines"),
         month   = factor(month))

model <- glm(late ~ period + airline + origin + month + rain + low_vis + strong_wind,
             data = model_data, family = binomial)

# Odds ratios: above 1 means more likely to leave late than the comparison group
odds <- tidy(model) |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "period|rain|low_vis|strong_wind|origin")) |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = round(exp(estimate), 2),
         ci_low     = round(exp(estimate - 1.96 * std.error), 2),
         ci_high    = round(exp(estimate + 1.96 * std.error), 2)) |>
  select(term, odds_ratio, ci_low, ci_high)
odds
```

Odds ratios are hard to explain to a manager, so the next step turns the model into plain percentages: what share of all flights would leave late if every flight were scheduled in the morning, or if it rained every hour, with everything else unchanged.

```{r what-if, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
what_if <- function(...) {
  newdata <- mutate(model_data, ...)
  round(100 * mean(predict(model, newdata = newdata, type = "response")), 1)
}
p <- function(x) factor(x, levels = levels(model_data$period))

scenarios <- tribble(
  ~factor,                       ~without,                          ~with,
  "Scheduled 6pm+ (vs 5-8am)",   what_if(period = p("5-8am")),      what_if(period = p("6pm+")),
  "Rain",                        what_if(rain = FALSE),             what_if(rain = TRUE),
  "Visibility under 3 miles",    what_if(low_vis = FALSE),          what_if(low_vis = TRUE),
  "Wind 20 mph or more",         what_if(strong_wind = FALSE),      what_if(strong_wind = TRUE)
) |>
  mutate(difference_pts = with - without,
         factor = fct_reorder(factor, difference_pts))
scenarios

p_model <- ggplot(scenarios, aes(y = factor)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = without, xend = with, yend = factor), colour = grey, linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = without), colour = navy, size = 4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = with), colour = orange, size = 4) +
  geom_text(aes(x = with, label = paste0(with, "%")), hjust = -0.4, size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(aes(x = without, label = paste0(without, "%")), hjust = 1.4, size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 40)) +
  labs(title = "Time of day moves the late rate more than any weather condition",
          subtitle = "Predicted late departures without (navy) and with (orange) each factor",
       x = "Predicted late departures (%)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Logistic regression on 406,779 NYC departures in 2023, controlling for airline, airport and month")
p_model
ggsave("charts/what_if.png", p_model, width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
```

After holding airline, airport, month and weather constant, time of day matters most. If every flight were scheduled between 5 and 8am, the model predicts 10.4% would leave late; if every flight left at 6pm or later, 32.1% would, three times as many. Rain adds 8.7 percentage points, low visibility 7.6 and strong wind 5.6. Weather makes individual days worse, but the timetable affects every flight: delays carried forward through the day by the same aircraft and crews are the bigger, and more controllable, problem.

## 6. Limitations

- The data covers one year and three airports; other years or cities may differ.
- Weather is measured at the airport in the scheduled hour. Storms elsewhere in the network, which can delay the incoming aircraft, are not included.
- The model shows associations. The evening effect most likely comes from delays carried forward through the day, but the data does not record the cause of each delay.
- Cancelled flights (2.5%) are left out of the late rate, so the worst disruptions are not counted as delays.
